lines: @@ -88,6 +88,7 @@ Performance improvements:

- Cache the hash of an AST node (`ASTHasher::hash()`) in a `WeakMap` instead of a dynamic property of the node. PHP allocates a property table of 376 bytes for the first dynamic property of an object, and the hash was the only dynamic property of most of the nodes that had one: in Phan's analysis of itself, 27 % of the nodes of an analyzed file had a dynamic property, and 5 % do now. The saving in peak memory is small (2 MB of 724 MB for that run), because few of those nodes are alive at the same time. A modified clone of a hashed node no longer keeps the hash of the original node ([#5638](https://github.com/phan/phan/issues/5638))
Bug fixes:

+- Don't split a doc comment type at the `&` of a literal string. `@return 'R&D'` was read as the literal string `'R,D'` (and `array{sep: '&'|'&'}` as `array{sep:','|',amp;'}`), so that returning `'R&D'` was reported as `PhanTypeMismatchReturnProbablyReal`: the type was split as an intersection type and the parts were joined with a comma.

- Don't report `PhanAbstractStaticMethodCall` for `$class::method()` when `$class` is a `class-string<Foo>` and `method()` is an abstract static method of the abstract class or interface `Foo`. Such a string is the name of a class that is a `Foo`, which implements the method. It is still reported when the variable can be the name of the abstract class itself (`$class = Foo::class;`), and for `Foo::method()`.

- Don't report `PhanAbstractStaticMethodCallInTrait` for `self::method()` and `static::method()` in a method of a trait that declares the abstract static method. In a trait, `self` and `static` are the class that uses the trait. The abstract method is only reached when the method of the trait is called on the trait itself, which is deprecated since PHP 8.1 and reported as `PhanCompatibleAccessMethodOnTraitDefinition` where it is done. This issue is no longer emitted.

- Don't assume the opposite of `@phpstan-assert-if-true`/`-false` (and the `@phan-` forms) for a type that Phan reads as a wider one: `numeric`, `numeric-string`, `literal-string`, `lowercase-string`, `class-string<Foo>` and its relatives, `int<1, 10>`, the value of a class constant, an array shape that can have other keys, and a type alias (which can stand for any of these). After `@phpstan-assert-if-true numeric-string $x`, a `?string` was `null` when the function returned false, although a string that is not numeric is still a string. The asserted type is still used for the result that the annotation names. A negated assertion of such a type (`!numeric-string $x`) is not used.
